correctness.rationale: The operator is compact via D(I-tS)^(-1), its nonzero eigenvalues are algebraically simple, and an exact biorthogonal vector pair yields rank-one spectral projections. Hardy Parseval and a circle automorphism prove the critical exact norm identity; a nondegenerate saddle and dominated series convergence respectively prove the fixed-positive-coupling and Bessel limits. Analyticity proves completeness; unbounded projection norms preclude every Schauder ordering and similarity to a spectral operator. Supplementary checker executes 2035 finite assertions and is not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The operator has unchanged simple positive eigenvalues for all 0<=t<1, yet its intrinsic Riesz projection condition numbers grow exponentially at every fixed t>0. The exact rate and prefactor, critical Bessel scaling, and obstruction to Schauder eigenbasis or scalar-type similarity quantify spectral instability that existing compactness/spectrum statements cannot detect. The scale m*t is canonical, not an arbitrary sliced invariant.
